summary: The Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI) is NOT a closed-list ban on pet rats - it's a permit pathway. Its Animal Quarantine rules (NMIAC T85-20.1) require a written entry permit for ALL animal imports from the Chief of Animal Health & Industry, but the only prohibited pet/guard mammals are a NAMED list (skunks, bats, raccoons, foxes, coyotes, wolves, wild/feral canids and felids and crosses) - NEITHER Rattus rattus NOR R. norvegicus appears on it. DLNR's own import page treats non-cat/dog animals as case-by-case ('email us, regulations vary by species'), and Customs classifies all animals as 'permits-required,' not prohibited. So a rat can be imported under an entry permit + a vet health certificate (rodents need no rabies vaccine), plus a DFW wildlife import permit ($10/species); once lawfully imported, keeping isn't separately restricted. Federal overlay: R. rattus (unlike the exempt R. norvegicus) needs a USFWS Form 3-177 wildlife declaration and must route through a designated port (Honolulu) or get a Designated Port Exception Permit. Breeding/intra-island transfer are simply unaddressed by CNMI law.

keep.why: Once a rat is lawfully imported under an entry permit, no CNMI statute prohibits keeping it - the T85-20.1 prohibited-pet-mammal list names only skunks/bats/raccoons/foxes/coyotes/wolves/wild canids+felids, not Rattus. CNMI PL 21-31 (cruelty/theft) doesn't restrict rat ownership.
keep.governing_law: NMIAC T85-20.1 (Animal Quarantine; entry permit; named-prohibited list excludes Rattus); NMIAC T85-30.1 (DFW import permit); CNMI PL 21-31; 50 CFR Part 14 (USFWS Form 3-177).

breed.why: No CNMI law addresses private captive breeding of pet rodents; the permit scheme governs import, not domestic breeding. The DFW non-native-release prohibition is an indirect constraint if stock escaped. Closed-colony breeding from lawfully-imported animals appears outside any specific prohibition but isn't affirmatively authorized - confirm with DLNR.
breed.governing_law: NMIAC T85-20.1 (Animal Quarantine; entry permit; named-prohibited list excludes Rattus); NMIAC T85-30.1 (DFW import permit); CNMI PL 21-31; 50 CFR Part 14 (USFWS Form 3-177).

sell_give.why: No CNMI statute specifically prohibits or permits intra-island sale/transfer of captive-born pet rats; the DFW permit regime is for import/export, and the cruelty law governs treatment, not sale. No commercial-pet licensing framework identified - confirm with DLNR.
sell_give.governing_law: NMIAC T85-20.1 (Animal Quarantine; entry permit; named-prohibited list excludes Rattus); NMIAC T85-30.1 (DFW import permit); CNMI PL 21-31; 50 CFR Part 14 (USFWS Form 3-177).

transport.why: Import requires an entry permit from the Chief of Animal Health & Industry (advance inquiry; permit fee; USDA-accredited vet health certificate within 10 days; rodents need no rabies vaccine) + a DFW wildlife import permit ($10/species). Federal: R. rattus needs a USFWS Form 3-177 + a USFWS-designated port (Honolulu) or a Designated Port Exception Permit (R. norvegicus is exempt). CNMI is outside US customs territory but USFWS/APHIS/CDC apply. Never release.
transport.governing_law: NMIAC T85-20.1 (Animal Quarantine; entry permit; named-prohibited list excludes Rattus); NMIAC T85-30.1 (DFW import permit); CNMI PL 21-31; 50 CFR Part 14 (USFWS Form 3-177).

restrictions.summary: To bring a rat into CNMI: email DLNR Animal Health in advance, obtain an entry permit from the Chief of Animal Health & Industry + a USDA-accredited vet health certificate (within 10 days; no rabies vaccine for rodents), and a DFW wildlife import permit ($10/species). For R. rattus add a USFWS Form 3-177 + route via a designated port (Honolulu) or a Designated Port Exception Permit. Never release.
steps: Email CNMI DLNR Animal Health (cnmianimalhealth@gmail.com) with species/number/purpose
Obtain the entry permit + DFW import permit + USDA health certificate
For R. rattus: file USFWS Form 3-177 + designated-port/DPEP
restrictions.where_to_file: CNMI DLNR - Division of Agriculture, Animal Health Section

inquiry_focus: (1) Are domestically-bred pet rats (Rattus norvegicus and Rattus rattus) eligible for an animal entry permit under NMIAC T85-20.1, and what documentation/health-certificate/quarantine requirements apply specifically to pet rats? (2) Does the Chief of Animal Health & Industry have discretion to permit pet rodent species not named in the prohibited-animal list (which covers only skunks/bats/raccoons/foxes/coyotes/wolves/wild canids+felids)? (3) Are separate permits required from BOTH the Animal Health Section and the Division of Fish & Wildlife ($10/species), or does one entry permit suffice?
